projects.name: Freqtrade + FreqAI
projects.what_it_does: Crypto trading bot (CCXT exchanges) with a built-in ML layer (FreqAI): user defines features (feature_engineering_*) and targets (set_freqai_targets) in the strategy; FreqAI slides a train window, trains LightGBM/XGBoost/CatBoost/PyTorch MLP/Transformer/SB3 RL, predicts the next backtest window, retrains live every live_retrain_hours, and adds outlier/drift filters (SVM, DBSCAN, Dissimilarity Index, PCA). Has Telegram bot integration out of the box.
projects.validation_audit: Split/retraining: freqtrade/freqai/data_kitchen.py:316-380 split_timerange() builds strictly sequential windows: train = train_period_days, backtest = the backtest_period_days immediately after, window slides by bt_period. freqai_interface.py:348-352 truncates the frame at tr_train.stopdt BEFORE calling set_freqai_targets(), so shift(-N) labels of the last N training candles become NaN and are dropped: no label spill from the backtest window into training (good; better than most hobby repos). Live: data_kitchen.py:533-583 check_if_new_training_required() retrains when elapsed > live_retrain_hours on the last train_period_days. Internal train/test split (data_kitchen.py:124-160) uses sklearn train_test_split with shuffle forced False (line 136) and test_size default 0.25 (docs/freqai-configuration.md:28), i.e. the tail of the train window; NO purge/embargo between train tail and test head, so the internal validation/early-stopping metric is mildly optimistic (labels of last train rows overlap first test rows). shuffle_after_split / reverse_train_test_order flags exist (lines 167-190) and would make the internal metric meaningless if a user enables them. Scalers (MinMax, PCA, DI) are fit on train only via feature_pipeline.fit_transform then transform on test/predict (base_models/BaseRegressionModel.py:56-79, freqai_interface.py:1027-1044): correct. Leak vector left to the user: indicators are populated once over the whole backtest timerange (freqai_interface.py:340-343), so any full-series normalisation in feature_engineering_* leaks (docs admit this). Costs: freqtrade backtester applies exchange taker fee from config or worst-case exchange tier (freqtrade/optimize/backtesting.py:270-281, 973); no slippage model, fills at candle open/limit assumptions. Results are OOS in the walk-forward sense but the backtest windows are contiguous with no embargo; no PBO/DSR-style multiple-testing control; hyperopt on the same data is the usual overfit path.
projects.reuse: Ideas to borrow (GPL blocks code copying into our paid service unless we AGPL/GPL our stack): (1) the 'truncate frame before computing targets' trick to kill window-boundary label leakage; (2) Dissimilarity Index (freqtrade/freqai/utils + datasieve DissimilarityIndex): distance of live features to the training set as a per-signal confidence/abstain gate; (3) fit_live_predictions (freqai_interface.py:725-741): fit a Gaussian to the last N predictions and only signal beyond mean +/- k*std, i.e. adaptive thresholds instead of fixed ones; (4) live_retrain_hours/train_period_days/expiration_hours as the config vocabulary for our retrain scheduler; (5) shuffle-forced-False default is a good sanity check. Do NOT adopt as a runtime: GPL-3, and its target is single-exchange bot execution, not a multi-user signal service.
projects.leak_or_red_flags: No hard leak in the default path. Soft issues: no purge between internal train/test tail split (data_kitchen.py:145-156); shuffle_after_split option; indicators computed on full range; no slippage model; GPL-3.

projects.name: Microsoft Qlib
projects.what_it_does: AI-oriented quant research platform: expression-based factor engine (Alpha158/Alpha360), DataHandler with learn/infer processor pipelines, 25+ benchmarked models (LightGBM, TRA, HIST, Transformer, TFT...), rolling retraining (qlib/contrib/rolling), concept-drift adaptation (DDG-DA meta-controller), portfolio backtest with TopkDropoutStrategy, MLflow recorders, RL for order execution.
projects.validation_audit: Labels: qlib/contrib/data/handler.py:90,152 label = Ref($close,-2)/Ref($close,-1)-1, i.e. next-next-day return, deliberately skipping one bar so the signal at t can be executed at t+1 close: honest execution-lag label. Normalisers require fit_start_time/fit_end_time and the code comments explicitly say fit_end_time must not include test data (qlib/data/dataset/processor.py:197-205); benchmark yaml sets fit_end_time=2014-12-31 = train end, segments train 2008-2014 / valid 2015-2016 / test 2017-2020 (examples/benchmarks/LightGBM/workflow_config_lightgbm_Alpha158.yaml:5-10, 53-56). CSZScoreNorm on the label is cross-sectional per date (learn-only), so no temporal leak. Task generator qlib/workflow/task/gen.py:305 (RollingGen/horizon) carries a label_leak_n parameter and truncates the train segment by the label horizon: purge is a first-class concept. Costs: exchange defaults open_cost 0.15% / close_cost 0.25% / min_cost 5 (qlib/backtest/exchange.py:48-50), benchmark uses 0.05%/0.15%; limit_threshold 9.5% models A-share limit-up/down; deal_price=close. Results are strictly OOS on the test segment, but valid+test are single fixed splits per benchmark, no CPCV/PBO. Crypto: scripts/data_collector/crypto is Coingecko daily-only and README says it cannot be used for backtesting (no OHLC): we would have to load our own dumps.
projects.reuse: Adopt selectively (MIT is clean): (1) copy the 'skip one bar' label convention Ref(close,-2)/Ref(close,-1) into signal_lab labels for 4h bars (predict return from next-bar open/close, not from current close); (2) port RollingGen's label_leak_n/horizon purge logic (qlib/workflow/task/gen.py:305-345) as a check against our purged walk-forward; (3) the DataHandlerLP learn_processors vs infer_processors split with fit_start/fit_end is the cleanest pattern for stateful transforms, replicate in our feature pipeline; (4) DDG-DA (examples/benchmarks_dynamic/DDG-DA) is worth a read for regime-drift-aware sample weighting, directly relevant to our HMM regimes; (5) Alpha158 expression list as a feature bank for LightGBM meta-labeling (cross-sectional factors matter less for 1-10 coins, so cherry-pick the time-series ones). Not worth adopting the whole platform: A-share daily-centric, heavy, dumps needed for crypto intraday.
projects.leak_or_red_flags: No leaks found in defaults; the leak risk is user misconfiguring fit_end_time. Benchmarks use a single fixed test split; crypto support is daily Coingecko only, no OHLC.

projects.name: Microsoft RD-Agent / RD-Agent(Q)
projects.what_it_does: LLM multi-agent loop that proposes factor hypotheses, writes factor code (CoSTEER), runs Qlib backtests in Docker, reads IC/annualized return/max drawdown, and feeds them back to the LLM to evolve the next hypothesis. RD-Agent(Q) (NeurIPS 2025) jointly optimises factors and models; paper claims ~2x annualized return vs Alpha360 with 70% fewer factors on CSI300.
projects.validation_audit: rdagent/scenarios/qlib/developer/feedback.py:17-21 IMPORTANT_METRICS = IC, 1day.excess_return_with_cost.annualized_return, ...max_drawdown; these are read from the Qlib recorder (rdagent/scenarios/qlib/experiment/factor_template/read_exp_res.py) whose backtest window is the TEST segment (factor_template/conf_baseline.yaml:50-52 backtest start_time = test_start, default 2017-01-01; segments valid 2015-2016, test 2017-). So the hypothesis-evolution loop is selecting factors on test-period performance: every iteration is another draw on the hold-out, i.e. systematic data snooping inflating reported test IC. Defaults in rdagent/app/qlib_rd_loop/conf.py:77 train_start 2008. The paper (arXiv 2505.15155v2) responds to leakage criticism by re-running with train 2008-2021 / valid 2022-2023 / test 2024-2025 and hiding raw data from the LLM; the released code still uses the test-window backtest as feedback. Costs are Qlib's (with_cost metrics) so fees are included. IC deduplication threshold 0.99 (factor_runner.py:60-61) only removes near-duplicates, not multiple-testing inflation.
projects.reuse: Borrow the architecture only: hypothesis -> code -> backtest -> LLM feedback is exactly our 'Claude as judge' loop. If we automate factor search with Claude, we MUST fix what RD-Agent gets wrong: feed the LLM validation-window metrics, keep a locked test window, and charge each iteration against PBO/DSR (we already have these in signal_lab). The CoSTEER factor-coder prompts (rdagent/scenarios/qlib/prompts.yaml, factor_coder.py) are reusable templates for having Claude write pandas feature functions with unit checks. MIT, so code can be lifted.
projects.leak_or_red_flags: Selection-on-test: LLM loop iterates on metrics computed over the test segment (feedback.py:17-21 + factor_template/conf_baseline.yaml:50-52). Expect the headline 2x return to shrink badly on a truly untouched period.

projects.name: NautilusTrader
projects.what_it_does: Production-grade event-driven engine: identical strategy code for backtest and live, nanosecond clock, L1/L2/L3 order-book matching engine, fill/latency/fee models, adapters for Binance, Bybit, OKX, dYdX, Hyperliquid, IB, Databento, etc. No ML layer; it is the execution/backtest substrate.
projects.validation_audit: No labels or train/test logic (not an ML framework). Costs: FillModel with prob_fill_on_limit / prob_slippage (crates/execution/src/models/fill.rs, python/tests/unit/backtest/test_backtest_configs.py), StaticLatencyModel (crates/backtest tests), FeeModel with maker/taker per instrument (crates/backtest/tests/integration/fee_model.rs). Event-driven replay removes the look-ahead class of bugs common in vectorised backtests (orders can only see data already emitted). Look-ahead is still possible in user indicators, but not in the engine.
projects.reuse: Best candidate if we ever want a faithful bar/orderbook-level replay of our Telegram signals (entry/stop/target with realistic fills and fees) or later execute for users. LGPL allows use as an unmodified library in a closed paid service. Overkill for the current stage (signal-only product, 4h-3d horizon); keep on the radar for when we need a Bybit/Binance live adapter and a proper fill model. Our signal_lab could emit signals that a thin Nautilus strategy consumes for a 'realistic PnL' report.
projects.leak_or_red_flags: None found; heavy Rust build, large API surface, frequent breaking releases (MIGRATION_V2.md).

projects.name: Jesse
projects.what_it_does: Python crypto bot/backtester with strategy DSL, hyperparameter optimizer, and a new research toolkit: ML gather/train pipeline (record_features/record_label inside a strategy, sklearn training), rule significance testing (stationary bootstrap of signal-only next-bar returns), Monte Carlo (trade shuffling and synthetic candles), plus an MCP server for Claude/Codex.
projects.validation_audit: Labels: jesse/research/ml.py:52-140 gather_ml_data() runs a backtest and collects {time, features, label} points the strategy records itself, so label look-ahead is entirely up to the user's record_label placement (typically at trade close, timestamped at entry: fine if the split is by entry time). Split: ml.py:99-108 strict chronological cut at test_ratio, no shuffle, but no purge/embargo between train end and test start, and no walk-forward: a single split. Significance: rule_significance_testing/rule_significance.py docstring + bootstrap.py:11-30: signal-only backtest collects +1/-1/0 at each bar, next-bar returns are detrended (zero-centred) and a stationary (geometric block, mean length 10) bootstrap yields a p-value for H0 'expected next-bar detrended return <= 0'. This is a proper, if simple, White-style test. Costs: exchange fee from config (jesse/config.py:42,122,179), no slippage model (grep for slippage returns no simulation code). Backtests are in-sample unless the user splits candle ranges manually.
projects.reuse: MIT, so code can be copied. Lift jesse/research/rule_significance_testing (stationary bootstrap with block resampling) as an additional placebo/significance test in signal_lab: it is complementary to our PBO/DSR (they test selection bias; this tests a single rule against a serial-dependence-preserving null). Also monte_carlo/monte_carlo_trades.py (trade-order reshuffling for drawdown distributions) is directly useful for the 'expected drawdown' line in Telegram. Their ML pipeline is simpler than ours (no purge, no calibration): nothing to take.
projects.leak_or_red_flags: ML split has no purge (ml.py:99-108); no slippage; label correctness delegated to user code.

projects.name: Kronos (financial K-line foundation model)
projects.what_it_does: Decoder-only transformer pre-trained on ~12B OHLCV bars from 45 exchanges (pretraining corpus ends June 2024 per paper/AAAI-2026). Tokenizer quantizes OHLCV into hierarchical tokens; autoregressive sampling gives multi-path price forecasts. Ships fine-tune pipeline on Qlib CSI300 with top-K backtest.
projects.validation_audit: Cloned /tmp/scout/Kronos. Fine-tune pipeline is mostly honest: finetune/dataset.py:104-114 z-scores each window using ONLY the lookback part (no future stats); splits are time-based (finetune/config.py:33-36); qlib backtest charges open_cost 0.1%, close_cost 0.15% (finetune/qlib_test.py:138) and reports with/without cost (:149-150). Signal = predicted close minus last close (qlib_test.py:277-282). Problems: (1) config.py:33-35 val range 2022-09..2024-06 overlaps train end 2022-12 and test range 2024-04..2025-06 overlaps val end 2024-06 — model selection sees ~3 months of test; (2) released pretrained weights saw data up to 2024-06, so any 'zero-shot' test before that is in-sample, and the repo's own test range starts 2024-04 (inside pretraining); (3) README:306 admits the top-K backtest ignores slippage/impact. Independent 5-min BTC test (1023jack.com, 249 OOS trades, chronological split): Kronos Brier 0.189 vs Brownian baseline 0.188 — indistinguishable. Paper reports RankIC lift vs generic TSFMs, not net-of-cost profitability.
projects.reuse: Do NOT use as the direction signal (no measurable edge on BTC OOS). Borrow: (a) the per-window lookback-only normalization pattern (dataset.py:104-114) as the template for any NN features in signal_lab; (b) its sampled multi-path forecasts as a cheap, honest *distribution* feature (predicted range / quantile spread over 4h–3d horizon) fed to meta-labeling, evaluated with our purged walk-forward and only on data after 2024-06 (pretraining cutoff). MIT is fine for a paid service. Treat Kronos-large (closed) as unavailable.
projects.leak_or_red_flags: Val/test date-range overlap in finetune/config.py:33-35; pretraining data through 2024-06 makes pre-2024-07 evaluations in-sample; no slippage in backtest; independent BTC test shows zero edge vs random walk.

projects.name: TradingAgents (TauricResearch, v0.5.x)
projects.what_it_does: Multi-agent LLM 'trading firm' (analysts → bull/bear debate → trader → risk debate → PM) built on LangGraph. v0.3–0.5 (2026) added point-in-time filters for news/fundamentals/FRED and a backtest sweep over a ticker×date grid that scores decisions after a holding window.
projects.validation_audit: Cloned /tmp/scout/TradingAgents. Point-in-time is real for data feeds: tools.py:34,58 clamp windows with as_of(); reddit.py:38-47 drops posts after end_date; CHANGELOG:176-190 & 233-240 document fixed look-ahead in FRED vintages, StockTwits/Reddit, Alpha Vantage fundamentals, memory recall (trading_graph.py:147). Backtest is NOT a backtest: backtest.py:88-90 scores hit-rate only for Buy/Sell/Over/Underweight, Hold is unscored; memory/settlement.py:52-74 measures close-to-close raw return minus SPY over holding_days=5, no fees/slippage, no position sizing, no equity curve; backtest.py:123-125 itself says 'one model sampling per cell, text feeds are not archived… indicative rather than repeatable'. No control for LLM parametric knowledge — any backtest date before the backbone's cutoff is contaminated (paper's Jan–Mar 2024 window is inside GPT-4o training). Original paper: 3 tickers, 3 months. Independent reproduction (trading-agents-lab, below) with anonymized prompts and 10 bps costs: agents −0.9% vs buy&hold +15.7% on AAPL Q2-2026.
projects.reuse: Do not adopt as signal engine (cost: ~$3–4 in LLM calls per decision, no demonstrated edge, unrepeatable). Borrow: the as_of()/as_of_window() vendor-clamp pattern (dataflows/date_window + tools.py) for our news/on-chain inputs, and the 'settle after holding window vs benchmark' idea for a live signal scoreboard in the bot (we already have hit/expectancy tracking — add benchmark-relative alpha). Also the Bull/Bear debate prompt structure could serve as a Claude-as-judge template, but judged only post-cutoff and forward.
projects.leak_or_red_flags: Backtest without costs, hit-rate excludes Hold, single LLM sample, LLM knowledge-cutoff leakage unaddressed; 109k stars ≠ evidence.

projects.name: trading-agents-lab (rigorous TradingAgents reproduction)
projects.what_it_does: Faithful reimplementation of TradingAgents plus the quant harness the paper lacked: 11.5y × 10 tickers, anonymized prompts (ticker/date masked, prices rebased to 100, volume as % avg), 10 bps costs always on, LightGBM expanding-window walk-forward with embargo as baseline, 62 tests incl. no-lookahead perturbation tests, cached deterministic LLM calls.
projects.validation_audit: Cloned /tmp/scout/trading-agents-lab. src/tradinglab/backtest/engine.py:3-5 'ONLY place signals are shifted', :50 position = sig.shift(1), :54-56 turnover cost 10 bps. models/ml.py:74-107 embargo = max(embargo_days, horizon) with explicit warning about label overlap. features/dataset.py:108 forward label shift(-horizon). README:289-308 lists survivorship bias, residual memorization risk, snapshot fundamentals. Results: anonymized agent desk −0.9% (Sharpe −1.21) vs B&H +15.7% on AAPL Mar–Jun 2026 (n=64 days, one ticker — authors say 'methodology demo'); LightGBM walk-forward L/S 2021+ : −19% cum (Sharpe −0.51), long-only +76% (Sharpe 0.48); turnover 0.35–0.69/day at 10 bps eats 9–17%/yr. Adversarial review fixed 17 issues (embargo gaps, drawdown/Sortino math, cost errors, warm-up phantom positions, anonymization channels).
projects.reuse: Adopt the methodology, not the agent: (1) anonymization v2 recipe (rebased index, % volume, masked dates) for any Claude-as-judge evaluation so we measure skill vs recall; (2) the 'delta between named and anonymized prompts = leak' probe (README roadmap item 1); (3) the single-shift-point rule and perturbation tests (tests/test_engine.py) as a CI pattern for signal_lab. Its finding that daily turnover kills LightGBM edge after 10 bps matches our 51–55% conclusion and argues for our slow-trend/4h–3d horizon.
projects.leak_or_red_flags: None found in code; honest limitations section. Tiny project (0 stars, 13 commits) — use as reference, not dependency.

projects.name: TLOB (Transformer for LOB price-trend prediction)
projects.what_it_does: DeepLOB successor: dual-attention transformer + MLPLOB on FI-2010, LOBSTER (TSLA/INTC) and a Kaggle BTC LOB dataset; 3-class trend labels at horizons of 10–100 LOB events; includes DeepLOB/BiN-CTABL baselines and a backtesting.py script.
projects.validation_audit: Cloned /tmp/scout/TLOB. Labels: utils/utils_data.py:127-161 compare mean of next h mid-prices vs mean of previous len mid-prices; threshold alpha = mean|pct_change|/2 computed over the WHOLE array passed in, and test labels are produced by calling labeling(test_input) (preprocessing/btc.py:153,163) — the class threshold for the test set is derived from test-set statistics (mild leak of test distribution into label definition; also forces balanced classes). Normalization is clean: z-score fit on train and reused (lobster.py:264-266, utils_data.py:11). Split is chronological by day 80/10/10 (btc.py:217-222, constants.py:70); FI-2010 uses the standard fixed test days (fi_2010.py:8-15). Backtest: run_backtesting.py:34 market_fee = 0, :246 Backtest(commission=0.00005) — 0.5 bps, far below any real crypto taker fee; strategy pyramids up to 31 orders. Paper itself concedes F1 collapses when trends are defined by the spread and that predictability declined (−6.68 F1 over years). Horizons are LOB events (seconds), i.e. sub-minute.
projects.reuse: Not usable for a 4h–3d Telegram service: signals live at event horizon and die under realistic fees (their own admission). Borrow only the 'threshold trend label from smoothed future-vs-past mean' idea if we ever want a 3-class variant of triple-barrier, but compute the threshold on train only and set it ≥ round-trip cost. Otherwise skip.
projects.leak_or_red_flags: Label threshold computed from the split being labeled incl. test (utils_data.py:152 via btc.py:153); backtest commission 0.5 bps and market_fee=0; sub-second horizon.
